Pool, Sun, and Salt Water: A Hair Type Expert's Guide to Summer Hair Survival
items.summary: Chlorine, salt water, and UV exposure can change the way your hair looks, feels, and behaves. The reason isn't random, and it affects every hair type. The way your hair responds to pool water, ocean water, and sun exposure depends on its hair type, cuticle structure, moisture retention patterns, and daily routine. Understanding those differences can help you build a routine that works with your hair instead of against it. Hair damage occurs when the protective, outer layer of your hair, also known as the cuticle, is compromised, leaving cracks in its exterior. Once cracked, the cuticle lifts, resulting in dull, dry, frizzy, or brittle hair. It can be a nightmare, but all hope is not lost! While you may not be able to completely repair hair that is already damaged, there are still plenty of steps you can take to help prevent it from happening in the future. Building Your Hair Type's Summer Defense The good news is that protecting your hair during the summer doesn't require a complicated routine. We created a bundle just for you: Summer Rescue Bundle. This 3-step smoothing system is designed to help improve the feel of rough, dry, and hard-to-manage hair. One of the factors that can contribute to these conditions is chlorine exposure, which can affect moisture balance and leave strands feeling coarse. Formulated with hydrating ingredients, this system helps support hydration at the cuticle level, restoring softness, strengthening hair, improving manageability, and making hair feel smoother. A few simple steps before and after swimming can help support moisture retention, improve manageability, and reduce the effects of repeated environmental exposure What Chlorine, Salt Water, and Sun Actually Do to Hair Hair is made primarily of protein called keratin and protected by an outer layer called the cuticle. The cuticle acts as the hair's first line of defense, helping regulate moisture retention and protecting the inner structure of the fiber. Chlorine weakens keratin, which is the structural protein that gives hair its elasticity, resulting in split ends and breakage. Exposure to saltwater and UV rays physically pulls moisture from your strands through osmosis, leaving them dehydrated. Salt acts as a sponge, pulling water out of the hair shaft, which gives it a parched, straw-like texture. When this happens, moisture can escape more easily, the hair surface may become rougher, and strands can appear drier, duller, or more prone to frizz. Color-treated hair may also experience faster fading when exposed to the sun and pool water. Using the right products can help reduce breakage and recover from the summer stressors that we put on our hair. The goal is to understand how your hair's structure responds to summer conditions and support it accordingly. Sun, Salt Water, and Chlorine Affect Every Hair Type Differently Hair type isn't just how your hair looks. It's how it functions. The shape of the hair fiber influences how oils travel, how moisture is retained, and how the hair responds to environmental stressors like chlorine, UV exposure, humidity, and salt water. Straight Hair To protect and repair straight hair from chlorine and saltwater, focus on lightweight hydration and smoothing the cuticle. Straight hair shows structural damage quickly through frizz, limpness, and a straw-like texture, but it also weighs down easily if you use products that are too heavy. Avoid rubbing your hair with heavy beach towels, which roughs up the hair cuticle and causes extreme frizz. Instead, gently blot your hair or wrap it in a soft microfiber towel or cotton t-shirt. Wavy Hair Wavy hair (Type 2) sits between straight and curly hair in terms of moisture distribution. The bends in the hair strand make it slightly harder for oils to travel evenly, which can make waves more susceptible to frizz and moisture loss during the summer months. Sun exposure, chlorine, and humidity can disrupt wave definition, leaving hair looking less uniform and more prone to expansion. For wavy hair, protecting your pattern means balancing heavy moisture retention with curl-safe detangling. Wavy hair is naturally more porous and prone to frizz than straight hair, meaning chlorine and salt water can completely flatten your wave definition and turn your texture coarse or stringy. Curly Hair Curly hair (Type 3) naturally experiences greater challenges with moisture distribution because oils must travel around multiple curves and bends in the hair fiber. Protecting your curls from chlorine and saltwater is all about maximizing moisture barriers and preventing severe shrinkage and matting. Curly hair (Type 3) is naturally highly porous, meaning it absorbs damaging pool chemicals and salt like a sponge, leading to extreme frizz and hair damage. Coily Hair Coily hair (Type 4) has the most complex strand geometry of all hair types, making moisture retention especially important. Because natural oils have the hardest time traveling from root to end, coily hair often relies heavily on conditioning and moisture-focused routines to maintain softness and manageability. After swimming or prolonged sun exposure, coily hair may experience increased dryness and require additional hydration to help support the cuticle and maintain moisture balance. 4-Step Pre-swim Prep Routine before stepping into the water: Saturate with fresh water: Soak your hair completely under a tap or beach shower. Hair acts like a sponge; filling it with clean water prevents it from absorbing chemical pool water or drying salt water. Apply a leave-in conditioner: Coat your damp strands from roots to tips to create a water-resistant barrier. Use a leave-in conditioner built for your hair type. Put hair in a protective style: Secure your hair to minimize water friction, tangles, and matting. Use a high bun for straight hair, loose braids for wavy hair, and tight twists for curly hair. Wear a silicone swim cap: For the ultimate protection, tuck your prepped hair inside a silicone swim cap. This physically blocks the majority of the water from ever touching your strands. The best summer routine isn't about fighting your hair. It's about supporting the way your hair naturally functions so it can better withstand everything summer throws at it. Post-swim Routine for Your Hair Type (Straight, Curly, Coily, Wavy) Straight Hair: Focus on Cleansing With Lightweight Moisture Straight hair typically distributes natural oils more efficiently from root to end, which helps support shine and smoothness. After repeated swims and frequent washing, however, that natural lubrication can be reduced, leaving hair looking duller or feeling dry at the ends. After swimming, cleanse with the Straight Hair Shampoo to remove chlorine, salt, sunscreen, and buildup without stripping moisture. Follow with the Straight Hair Conditioner, formulated with coconut water and avocado oil to help support softness and shine. If you're spending extended time outdoors, apply Custom Styling Primer before styling to help provide heat and UV protection. Formulated with a Style Defense Complex that protects against heat and UV up to 450°F, with your choice of hair goals built in. Delivers up to 24 hours of humidity and frizz control without leaving a crunchy texture.Color & UV Defense: Formulated with rice seed protein to defend hair color from fading and protect strands from sun-induced UV damage. Wavy Hair: Focus on Moisture Balance and Definition Wavy hair sits in the middle of the moisture spectrum. It can become oily at the roots while still experiencing dryness through the mid-lengths and ends. Summer conditions often amplify frizz and make waves lose their natural definition. After swimming, use the Wavy Hair Shampoo to gently cleanse away chlorine and saltwater residue. Follow with the Wavy Hair Conditioner, featuring fermented rice water and argan oil to help support hydration without weighing waves down. For styling, apply Zero Gravity Styling Mousse to damp hair. Our lightweight foam mousse creates a flexible hold that's never crunchy, enhances the volume of your natural waves while keeping hair frizz-free. Aloe juice and apple extract help encourage wave definition while reducing the puffiness that often follows a day in the sun or water. Curly Hair: Focus on Moisture Retention and Curl Definition Curly hair naturally experiences greater challenges with moisture distribution because oils must travel around bends and curves throughout the strand. When chlorine, salt water, and sun exposure enter the equation, curls may feel drier, less defined, and more prone to tangling. After swimming, cleanse with the Curly Hair Shampoo and follow with the Curly Hair Conditioner. Ingredients like flaxseed and Brazilian pracaxi oil help support hydration and manageability while encouraging curl definition. To help curls recover after a day in the water, apply Super Shape Curl Cream to damp hair. Moringa oil and sugarcane help support curl formation while improving softness and reducing tangles. Coily Hair: Focus on Hydration and Recovery Coily hair has the most complex strand geometry, making moisture retention a priority year-round. Because natural oils have the hardest time traveling from root to end, repeated exposure to chlorine, salt water, and sun can leave coils feeling particularly dry if moisture isn't replenished. After swimming, cleanse with the Coily Hair Shampoo and follow with the Coily Hair Conditioner, formulated with chia seed and Jamaican black castor oil to help support hydration and softness. Between wash days, use the Custom Co-Wash to gently cleanse the scalp and hair without removing the moisture your coils need to stay manageable. Formulated with Jamaican black castor seed oil and avocado oil, this co-wash moisturizes and protects coily, curly, and color-treated hair. If you'll be spending long days outdoors, apply Super Shape Curl Creme before going into the elements. Our Curly Hair Super Shape Curl Cream defines and hydrates curls with a flexible, touchable hold that never feels crunchy or sticky. This lightweight, plant-based cream enhances your natural curl pattern while reducing frizz and boosting elasticity for smooth, bouncy curls that last. Formulated with Castor Seed Oil and Moringa Oil for softness and shine, plus Hemisqualane to protect against breakage and humidity. The Bottom Line Summer is hard on hair, but it doesn't have to be a mystery. Try the Summer Rescue Bundle. and get 20% off with code: SummerRescue. This 3-step smoothing system is designed to help improve the feel of rough, dry, and hard-to-manage hair. One of the factors that can contribute to these conditions is chlorine exposure, which can affect moisture balance and leave strands feeling coarse. Formulated with hydrating ingredients, this system helps support hydration at the cuticle level, restoring softness, strengthening hair, improving manageability, and making hair feel smoother. Sun and chlorine create specific, structural stress, and your hair type determines exactly how that stress shows up and what it needs to recover. That's the difference between guessing at a "summer hair fix" and actually knowing your hair's structure well enough to protect it. It's as easy as- Find your hair type, build your Summer Rescue Bundle, and let the rest of summer be about the pool, not the dry hair.
